children.name: Zelkova carpinifolia  K.Koch
children.description: Zelkova carpinifolia, known as Caucasian zelkova, Caucasian elm or just zelkova, is a species of Zelkova, native to the Caucasus, Kaçkar, and Alborz mountains of eastern Europe and southwest Asia.

children.name: Zelkova sicula
children.description: Zelkova sicula is a species of Zelkova in the family Ulmaceae.

children.name: Zelkova abelicea
children.description: Zelkova abelicea is a species of tree in the family Ulmaceae.

children.name: Zelkova schneideriana
children.description: Zelkova schneideriana, the Chinese zelkova (a name it shares with other members of its genus), is a species of flowering plant in the family Ulmaceae.

children.name: Zelkova serrata
children.description: Zelkova serrata (Japanese zelkova, Japanese elm, keyaki, or keaki; or ; ; ) is a species of the genus Zelkova native to Japan, Korea, eastern China and Taiwan.

children.name: Zelkova sinica
children.description: Zelkova sinica, the Chinese zelkova, is a species of flowering plant in the family Ulmaceae, native to central and southeastern China.

children.name: Phyllostylon
children.description: Phyllostylon — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Phyllostylon rhamnoides
children.description: The native range of this species is Mexico to Trop. America. It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Holoptelea
children.description: Holoptelea — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Holoptelea integrifolia
children.description: Holoptelea integrifolia, the Indian elm or jungle cork tree, is a species of tree in the family Ulmaceae, and a close relative to the true elms (Ulmus).

children.name: Holoptelea grandis
children.description: The native range of this species is W. Trop. Africa to Uganda. It is a tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Hemiptelea
children.description: Hemiptelea — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Hemiptelea davidii
children.description: The native range of this species is China to Korea. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Planera
children.description: Planera — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Planera aquatica J.F.Gmel.
children.description: Planera aquatica, the planertree or water elm, is a species of flowering plant.

children.name: Ulmus
children.description: Ulmus — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Ulmus boissieri Grudz.
children.description: The native range of this species is W. & SW. Iran. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus changii W.C.Cheng
children.description: Ulmus changii, occasionally known as the Hangzhou elm, is a small deciduous tree found across much of China in forests at elevations of up to 1800 m.

children.name: Ulmus chenmoui W.C.Cheng
children.description: The native range of this species is China (Anhui, Jiangsu). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus chumlia Melv. & Heybr.
children.description: Ulmus chumlia is a small deciduous tree endemic to the Himalaya from the Kashmir to central Nepal, and the provinces of Yunnan, Sichuan and Xizang (Tibet) in China.

children.name: Ulmus elliptica K.Koch
children.description: Ulmus elliptica Koch (named for the elliptic samara ) is a disputed species of elm, native to the Caucasus, where Koch reported (1849, 1872) that it formed extensive woods, and ranging north to southern Ukraine.

children.name: Ulmus elongata L.K.Fu & C.S.Ding
children.description: Ulmus elongata, also known as the long raceme elm in the US, is a deciduous tree endemic to broadleaf forests in the eastern provinces of China.

children.name: Ulmus erythrocarpa W.C.Cheng ex Yi F.Duan & X.R.Wang
Ulmus harbinensis S.Q.Nie & G.Q.Huang
children.description: Ulmus harbinensis Nie & Huang , also known as the Harbin elm, is a small elm found only in the province of Heilongjiang in the northeastern extremity of China, where it occurs in mixed forest.

children.name: Ulmus ismaelis Todzia & Panero
children.description: Ulmus ismaelis is a small tree discovered circa 1997 in southern Mexico by Ismael Calzada in riparian forest along the Mixteco River system in northeastern Oaxaca, where it grows among large boulders in the limestone canyons.

children.name: Ulmus kunmingensis W.C.Cheng
children.description: The native range of this species is SC. China (to Guangxi). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus lamellosa Z.Wang & S.L.Chang
children.description: Ulmus lamellosa, commonly called the Hebei elm, is a small deciduous tree native to four Chinese provinces, Hebei, Henan, Nei Mongol, and Shanxi, to the west and south of Beijing.

children.name: Ulmus macrocarpa Hance
children.description: Ulmus macrocarpa Hance , the large-fruited elm, is a deciduous tree or large shrub endemic to the Far East excluding Japan.

children.name: Ulmus microcarpa L.K.Fu
children.description: Ulmus microcarpa was named and first described by the Chinese botanist L.

children.name: Ulmus mossii A.Henry ex J.V.Armstr. & P.D.Sell, 2018
Ulmus prunifolia W.C.Cheng & L.K.Fu
children.description: The native range of this species is China (Chongqing, W. Hubei). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus uyematsui Hayata
children.description: Ulmus uyematsui Hayata , commonly known as the Alishan elm, is endemic to forests at elevations of in Alishan, Chiayi County [http://itouchmap.com/?c=tw&UF=-2626874&UN=-3624130&DG=MTS], central Taiwan, where it is considered one of the minor tree species.

children.name: Ulmus villosa Brandis ex Gamble
children.description: Ulmus villosa, the cherry-bark elm or Marn elm, is one of the more distinctive Asiatic elms, and a species capable of remarkable longevity.

children.name: Ulmus mexicana
children.description: Ulmus mexicana, the Mexican elm, is a large tree endemic to Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Ulmus laevis
children.description: The native range of this species is Europe to W. Siberia and NW. Türkiye. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus rubra
children.description: Ulmus rubra, the slippery elm, is a species of elm native to eastern North America.

children.name: Ulmus pumila
children.description: Ulmus pumila, the Siberian elm, is a tree native to Asia.

children.name: Ulmus thomasii
children.description: Ulmus thomasii, the rock elm or cork elm (or orme liège in Québec), is a deciduous tree native primarily to the Midwestern United States.

children.name: Ulmus davidiana
children.description: Ulmus davidiana, also known as the David elm, or Father David elm (named after the botanist Armand David, who collected specimens), is a small deciduous tree widely distributed across China, Mongolia, Korea, Siberia, and Japan, where it is found in wetlands along streams at elevations of 2000–2300 m (6,500–7,500 ft).

children.name: Ulmus glaucescens
children.description: The native range of this species is China. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus parvifolia
children.description: Ulmus parvifolia, commonly known as the Chinese elm or lacebark elm, is a species native to eastern Asia, including China, India, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Siberia, and Kazakhstan.

children.name: Ulmus serotina
children.description: Ulmus serotina, the September elm, is an autumn-flowering North American species of tree.

children.name: Ulmus crassifolia
children.description: The native range of this species is C. & SE. U.S.A. to NE. Mexico. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus laciniata
children.description: Ulmus laciniata (Trautv.) Mayr , known variously as the Manchurian, cut-leaf, or lobed elm, is a deciduous tree native to the humid ravine forests of Japan, Korea, northern China, eastern Siberia and Sakhalin, growing alongside Cercidiphyllum japonicum, Aesculus turbinata, and Pterocarya rhoifolia, at elevations of 700–2200 m, though sometimes lower in more northern latitudes, notably in Hokkaido.

children.name: Ulmus castaneifolia
children.description: Ulmus castaneifolia Hemsley , the chestnut-leafed elm or multinerved elm, is a small deciduous tree found across much of China in broadleaved forests at elevations of .

children.description: Ulmus bergmanniana C.K.Schneid.

children.name: Ulmus gaussenii
children.description: The native range of this species is China (Anhui: Langya Shan). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Ulmus pseudopropinqua
children.description: Ulmus pseudopropinqua Wang & Li , occasionally known in the United States as the Harbin spring elm, is a small deciduous tree found only in Heilongjiang, the northeasternmost province in China.

children.name: Ulmus szechuanica
children.description: Ulmus szechuanica Fang , known as the Szechuan (Sichuan), or red-fruited, elm, is a small to medium deciduous Chinese tree found along the Yangtze river through the provinces of Sichuan, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangsu.

children.name: Ulmus lanceifolia
children.description: Ulmus lanceifolia, occasionally known as the Vietnam elm, is a very large tree endemic to a wide area of southern Asia.

children.name: Ulmus wallichiana
children.description: The native range of this species is E. Afghanistan to Nepal. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.
